---
title: "Figure 6B (whole ladder) — distortion versus the memory left in the least-squares residual, one panel per member"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
VARIANT of figure_6B.Rmd, 2026-08-10, at Luciano's request: all eight members, each in its own panel,
in cost-ladder order. Design unchanged from figure_6B.Rmd, and the note there owns the reasoning.

THE X IS THE SAME FOR EVERY PANEL and it is tau_int of the LEAST-SQUARES residual, not of the member
being drawn. That is deliberate and it is the whole point of the figure: the reader measures this
number from the fit they were going to make anyway, before choosing a method, and then reads what
each member would do to their error bars at that x.

EACH PANEL HAS ITS OWN Y SCALE (Luciano, 2026-08-10). The members span four orders of magnitude
between them, from IR inside 0.98-1.08 to NR reaching 2217, and a shared axis flattens the four
recursive panels into a line at 1. The cost is that panel heights are no longer comparable by eye,
so the horizontal line at 1 is the only common reference and every panel keeps it.

COVERAGE IS NOT UNIFORM. IR carries 294 cells in the source data against 210 for the others, and the
join to the least-squares tau_int keeps only cells where both exist, so IR loses its extra cells
here. Panels therefore hold the same 210 cells apiece; the count is printed below so a reader of the
code can check it rather than assume it.

Labels follow figure_4.Rmd:329.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

LAB <- c(nonlinearsqr_g = "LSE", nonlinearsqr = "ILSE",
         macro_NR = "NR", macro_INR = "INR",
         macro_R = "R", macro_MR = "MR", macro_VR = "VR", macro_IR = "IR")

tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo == "nonlinearsqr") %>%
  transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", algo %in% names(LAB)) %>%
  select(algo, param, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = m)

dat <- spec %>%
  inner_join(tau, by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), is.finite(aniso), mag > 0, aniso > 0) %>%
  mutate(lo = mag / aniso, hi = mag * aniso,
         member = factor(unname(LAB[algo]), levels = unname(LAB)),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))))

cat(sprintf("figure_6B_all: %d marks; per member: %s\n", nrow(dat),
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(dat$member), as.integer(table(dat$member))),
                  collapse = " ")))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 4.8}
g <- ggplot(dat, aes(tau_int, mag, colour = d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ member, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20),
                labels = c("1", "1.5", "2", "3", "5", "10", "20")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(Delta*t %.% k[off]), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(x = expression("memory left in the least-squares residual,  "*tau[int]),
       y = "distortion of the reported information\n(point = size, bar = across directions)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8))

ggsave("Figure_6B_all.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 4.8, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
dat %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            size_med = median(mag), size_min = min(mag), size_max = max(mag),
            shape_med = median(aniso), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nfraction of cells with size >= 1.15, by member:\n")
dat %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), frac_distorted = mean(mag >= 1.15), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```
